attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

% Appendix
%=============================================================================

\section{Implementation Details}
\label{app:implementation}

This section provides the complete training configuration and architectural details for reproducing \ours{}.

\subsection{Model Architecture}

\ours{} builds on $\pi_{0.5}$ (openpi), a flow-matching Vision-Language-Action model comprising three components:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Vision encoder}: PaliGemma SigLIP-based vision encoder that processes RGB observations into visual tokens.
\item \textbf{Language model}: Gemma language backbone that fuses visual tokens with tokenized language instructions to produce a joint vision-language representation.
\item \textbf{Action expert}: Gemma-300M transformer that takes the vision-language context along with noisy action tokens and predicts velocity field outputs for flow-matching action generation. The action expert's output features have dimension $D = 1024$, which are projected to the action-space dimension $D_a = 32$ by a linear output layer.
\end{itemize}

The SDF auxiliary head is attached to the action expert's output projection layer via a PyTorch forward hook, requiring no modification to the base model's source code. The head architecture is:
\begin{equation}
\text{Linear}(1024, 256) \to \text{ReLU} \to \text{Linear}(256, 1)
\end{equation}
totaling 262,657 parameters ($< 0.09$\% of the action expert). The head is discarded after training and does not participate in inference.

\subsection{Training Configuration}
\label{app:training}

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\small
\caption{Training hyperparameters.}
\begin{tabular}{ll}
\toprule
Hyperparameter & Value \\
\midrule
Base model & $\pi_{0.5}$ (openpi) \\
Fine-tuning strategy & Full (all parameters) \\
Optimizer & AdamW \\
Peak learning rate & $5 \times 10^{-5}$ \\
LR schedule & Linear warmup + cosine decay \\
Warmup steps & 10,000 \\
Total training steps & 30,000 \\
Effective batch size & 128 (64 per GPU $\times$ 2 GPUs, DDP) \\
Gradient clipping & Global norm, max\_norm $= 1.0$ \\
Save interval & Every 5,000 steps \\
EMA & Not used \\
Hardware & 2$\times$ NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 (96\,GB VRAM each) \\
Distributed strategy & PyTorch DDP with gradient averaging \\
Precision & bfloat16 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}


\paragraph{Gradient flow through the backbone.} A critical design choice is whether to allow gradients from the SDF losses to propagate back through the action expert. When $\hat{s} = \mathrm{SDFHead}(f_t)$ with $f_t$ treated as a leaf tensor (detached from the computation graph), the SDF losses train only the auxiliary head without influencing action generation. We enable gradient flow from the SDF head through the shared features $f_t$ into the action expert weights: the feature tensor captured by the forward hook is used without detachment, so that $\nabla_{f_t} \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SDF}}$ and $\nabla_{f_t} \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{col}}$ both contribute to the backbone parameter update.

\subsection{\ours{}-Specific Configuration}
\label{app:geosafe_config}

\small
\caption{\ours{} auxiliary head and loss hyperparameters.}
\begin{tabular}{ll}
\toprule
Hyperparameter & Value \\
\midrule
SDF head architecture & Linear(1024, 256) $\to$ ReLU $\to$ Linear(256, 1) \\
SDF head parameters & 262,657 \\
SDF loss weight ($\lambda_{\mathrm{SDF}}$) & 0.1 \\
Collision loss weight ($\lambda_{\mathrm{col}}$) & 0.01 \\
Collision threshold ($\delta$) & 0.02\,m (2\,cm) \\
Noise-aware sigmoid sharpness ($\alpha$) & 10 \\
Noise-aware sigmoid center ($t_0$) & 0.5 \\
Backbone gradient from SDF losses & True \\

SDF label coverage & 57/72 task variants ($\sim$77\%) \\
\bottomrule
